chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn Ja'far from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who consumes the wealth of his children. He said: 'No, unless he is compelled to do so, in which case he may consume from it in a good manner. And it is not suitable for the children to take anything from their father's wealth except with the father's permission.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father consume his children's wealth, and can children take their father's money?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of financial autonomy is balanced with familial duty, establishing that while a father may consume his children's wealth out of necessity, he must do so 'bil-ma'ruf' (in a dignified, non-exploitative manner). Conversely, children are strictly prohibited from taking their father's wealth without explicit permission, reinforcing the father's authority over his estate. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between voluntary gifts and necessary consumption in family financial relations.
